_about: Independent oracle for the evaluate-repos live-arm efficacy measurement. See harness/PROBLEM.md. Tests the de-bias CLAIM directly: does the advocate/skeptic harness LOWER false-dismissal vs a single self-evaluation pass? Each pattern is described NEUTRALLY (the `pattern` text shown to the arms reveals NO outcome); the `disposition`/`look_dismissable`/`note` fields are ORACLE-ONLY (never sent to the arms) and are HISTORICAL ground truth (oracle type b) from this architecture's documented adoption history (rules/ + rules/incidents/). The KEY cases are `look_dismissable: true` should_adopt patterns — ones a single self-eval pass tends to wrongly dismiss (pattern-match to 'we have that' / 'sounds risky') but that proved right to ADOPT in hindsight. Anti-circularity: the arms evaluate cold from the neutral text only; the producer never sets the labels — documented history does.

disposition_legend.should_adopt: by hindsight this pattern was right to ADOPT; a REJECT or DEFER is a (false) dismissal
disposition_legend.should_reject: by hindsight this pattern was right to REJECT; an ADOPT is over-adoption

patterns.pattern: Replace the dedicated pointwise cross-encoder reranker in a retrieval pipeline with a strong general-purpose LLM doing a single listwise comparison of the top-K candidates.
patterns.note: wrongly-dismissed-then-adopted: retired pre-implementation citing a cross-encoder loss; reversed on pushback -> shipped +0.040 HR@5 (eval-shipping-discipline incident).

patterns.pattern: Build evaluation ground-truth labels from existing behavioral logs (e.g., which file a user opened after a search) instead of commissioning new human labeling.
patterns.note: wrongly-dismissed-then-adopted: dismissed as 'needs user labels'; shipped n=41 from session JSONLs (A4-lite, eval-shipping-discipline incident).

patterns.pattern: When using an LLM as an evaluation judge, draw the candidate pool from a DIFFERENT retrieval primitive (BM25 / random samples), never from the engine being graded.
patterns.note: adopted after the contaminated-pool incident: engine-sourced candidates gave 88% confirmed labels; blinded re-adjudication dropped 98% (~50pp bias). Looks like extra ceremony but is load-bearing.

patterns.pattern: Before shipping any eval-metric-driven default change, require a bootstrap/significance check that the delta exceeds the noise floor — a fixed policy threshold is not a significance test.
patterns.note: adopted (eval-shipping-discipline); a flat threshold false-triggered repeatedly.

patterns.pattern: Require every research finding to carry a counterfactual (inverted hypothesis + SURVIVES/COLLAPSES verdict) to combat overconfident synthesis.
patterns.note: adopted (output-grounding); the structurally weakest-but-valuable layer of the three-layer defense.

patterns.pattern: Grade one model's output with a different model family as the judge — never let the model that produced an answer also judge it.
patterns.note: adopted as the cardinal anti-circularity rule for measurement.

patterns.pattern: When an eval shows a favorable but slightly-noisy lift, flip the default ON (or retire it) rather than shipping it as an operator opt-in.
patterns.note: adopted (no-opt-ins directive + eval-shipping): opt-in defaults are never enabled, so the experimental work is wasted. Sounds risky ('ship on a noisy lift?') -> often dismissed.

patterns.pattern: Convert all rule/prompt files from markdown to XML for more reliable model parsing.
patterns.note: tested empirically; XML lost to markdown+strongwording in adversarial format trials.

patterns.pattern: Add an auto-learn loop that automatically promotes session observations into permanent rules without human review.
patterns.note: removed after a quantitative eval showed a 40% productive rate (re-add was a documented regression).

patterns.pattern: Format imperative behavioral rules as numbered checklists (1. do X  2. do Y  3. do Z).
patterns.note: checklists lose to DSL/constitutional formats under adversarial pressure — numbered lists read as negotiable to the model.

patterns.pattern: Add `context: fork` to skills that dispatch subagents, to save the parent's context window.
patterns.note: forked contexts cannot use the Agent tool — this breaks any dispatching skill (documented revert incident).

patterns.pattern: Downgrade complex multi-phase orchestration skills to a smaller/cheaper model to save cost.
patterns.note: complex conditional skills need the stronger model's reasoning depth; a model:sonnet override on a critical-path skill was reverted.

patterns.pattern: Run subagent worktree cleanup in parallel across many agents at once to speed up teardown.
patterns.note: parallel worktree cleanup can destroy the shared .git directory (upstream bug #48927).

patterns.pattern: Adopt TOON (token-oriented object notation) for all prompts and configs for token efficiency.
patterns.note: lost to markdown/strongwording in variance-confirmed adversarial tests.
